questions.subject: Maths
questions.prompt: A triangle has a base of 20 cm and a height of 8 cm. Slow down and work through it step by step: what is its area?

block.label: Quick Recall
block.sub: Four options, one answer — keep it fast

questions.why: Area = ½ × base × height = ½ × 20 × 8 = 80 cm². Halving is the step that gets rushed and skipped.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.prompt: A closed cylinder has radius 5 cm and height 10 cm. What is its total surface area? (use π ≈ 3.14, round to 1 decimal place)

block.label: Scrub It
block.sub: Rub out the wrong answers with your finger

questions.why: Total surface area = 2πr² + 2πrh = 157.0 + 314.0 = 471.0 cm². Forgetting the two circular ends gives the smaller wrong values.

questions.subject: Science
questions.prompt: In a closed system, what happens to total mass during a chemical reaction?
questions.why: Mass is conserved in a closed system — atoms are rearranged, not created or destroyed, so total mass stays the same.

questions.subject: Science
questions.prompt: Name one sign that a chemical reaction has taken place.
questions.why: Signs of a chemical reaction include colour change, gas bubbles, heat change, or a solid (precipitate) forming.
